speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As we emerge from the COVID-19 pandemic, economic and geopolitical uncertainties are expected to weigh on the labour market.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To tackle these challenges, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) will redouble our efforts to expand opportunities, strengthen support and assurance, and foster fair, inclusive, and safe workplaces for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As part of the Forward Singapore exercise, MOM and the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) have been engaging Singaporeans from all walks of life.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Many are concerned about staying relevant and competitive, and having job opportunities that match their aspirations.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As our economy transforms, MOM will empower Singaporean workers to take charge of their careers and improve their career prospects and resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MOM has launched Jobs Transformation Maps to provide individuals with insights on how technology will affect their jobs and how they can proactively take measures to remain competitive and relevant.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Singaporeans can also tap on employment facilitation programmes by Workforce Singapore to chart out their career paths.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will be launching CareersFinder, a feature on the MyCareersFuture portal, to help workers plan for their next career move using data and artificial intelligence.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For workers who face displacement, we will help them in their job search.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For those inclined towards “hands-on” work, MOM will work with NTUC to professionalise skilled trades, to attract and retain more Singaporeans in such jobs through better salaries and clearer progression ladders.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have made headway in uplifting the image and attractiveness of skilled professions that work with the “heart”, such as nursing and early childhood education.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We must do likewise for trades that emphasise craft and skills mastery.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MOM also aims to build up a stronger local pipeline for corporate leadership positions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We want to see more Singaporeans becoming specialists and leaders in their chosen fields of our economy and growing their careers in Singapore and on the global stage.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MOM will also support employers to grow and transform.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Only with strong companies can we have a vibrant economy and good job opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To this end, we will support our local workforce to constantly improve, even as Singapore remains open to foreign manpower that complements locals.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Through COMPASS, we will encourage companies to build strong and diverse teams, with Singaporeans and skilled EP holders working alongside and learning from one another.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The COMPASS Shortage Occupation List allows firms to access applicants with highly specialised skills, while the Strategic Economic Priorities bonus facilitates applications from firms that support Singapore’s strategic priorities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will also support businesses that contribute to our strategic priorities with additional Work Permit and S Pass quotas via the Manpower for Strategic Economic Priorities scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our growth has been and must continue to be inclusive.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have made progress in looking after vulnerable workers and will press on with our efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will invest heavily to uplift the salaries and skills of lower-wage workers, and help them progress in their careers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have also enhanced the Workfare Income Supplement scheme to increase maximum payments and expand coverage to half a million lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: With the recently launched PW Mark, consumers and corporate buyers can play their part to support firms that pay progressive wages.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Seniors who want and are able to continue working should have maximum access to employment opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have been raising the retirement and re-employment ages progressively, and have extended the Senior Employment Credit and Part-time Re-employment Grant until 2025 to provide employers with wage offsets.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In addition, we have enhanced the Enabling Employment Credit to raise wage offsets to employers who hire unemployed persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have also introduced a new Uplifting Employment Credit to incentivise firms to hire ex-offenders.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Platform workers will also be able to seek formal representation and negotiate for their collective interests.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: A decade ago, about five in ten active CPF members were able to attain their cohort Basic Retirement Sum at age 55.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This has improved to almost seven in ten today and is expected to reach about eight in ten in 2027.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are undertaking a fundamental review of our policies for retirement adequacy under the Forward Singapore exercise.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ultimately, we seek to assure all Singaporeans that as long as they work and contribute consistently to their CPF, they will be able to meet their basic retirement needs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will also find ways to look after those who are unable to work consistently or who have a shorter runway of working years.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MOM will continue to foster fair, inclusive, and safe workplaces, shape workplace norms, and ensure an even playing field for all.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will also continue to shape the right norms to help make our workplace practices more flexible.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MOM must continue to be both pro-worker and pro-business.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will build on the strong foundation of tripartism to journey hand-in-hand, step-by-step with all workers and businesses towards a better future.
